key_insight: A shared PV forecasting model pretrained across sites and horizons can forecast at unseen stations without station-specific training.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a scalable way to forecast distributed PV fleets while reducing repeated model training and maintenance as stations are added.
method: Formulate forecasting as sequence completion using historical PV power, weather observations, future numerical weather predictions, and time encodings.
Compare forecast-aligned, generic, and mixed reconstruction pretraining objectives.
Use mixed reconstruction to balance forecasting accuracy, resilience to degraded weather predictions, and downstream adaptation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered 479 PV stations, including 139 spatially held-out sites, and horizons from 6 hours to 7 days; the mixed-reconstruction model outperformed the tested station-specific, shared, and generalist time-series baselines.
watch_item: Deployment requires compatible weather and PV data pipelines; transfer beyond the evaluated stations and operating conditions remains to be validated.
paper_title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting
